newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia Senate rejects Telstra bill changes.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia Senate rejects Telstra bill changes.

text.p: The Australian Senate on Tuesday voted down an attempt by the Australian Democrats minority party to amend the bill that would authorise the one-third sale of government telecoms carrier Telstra Corp Ltd.
The two key independents, on whom the government is relying to pass the bill, voted with the government.
Immediately after the vote, independent Brian Harradine moved his joint amendment with the government, which he foreshadowed on Thursday.

Harradine said last week that he and the government had agreed to delay the commencement date for the act to ensure that Telstra shares could not be sold before a committee looked at his suggestion that money be raised from the company by selling securities instead of equity.
Although he has not said so, the deal implies that he would support the bill in that amended form. Other government offers last week answered concerns held by both independents.

The Telstra bill is currently in the Senate's amendment mode, called the committee of the whole. After all amendments have been proposed and determined by vote, the bill is presented in its amended form to the Senate for a final vote.
